# dgghrd

> Reduces a pair of real matrices (A, B) to generalized upper Hessenberg.

<section class="intro">

form using orthogonal transformations.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgghrd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dgghrd';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgghrd( order, compq, compz, N, ilo, ihi, A, LDA, B, LDB, Q, LDQ, Z, LDZ ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `compq` | `"none" \| "initialize" \| "update"` | `'none'`, `'initialize'`, or `'update'` |
| `compz` | `"none" \| "initialize" \| "update"` | `'none'`, `'initialize'`, or `'update'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ilo` | `integer` | Ilo (1-based)<br>Rejects `ilo < 1` |
| `ihi` | `integer` | Ihi (1-based)<br>Rejects `ihi > N \|\| ihi < ilo - 1` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix A |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix B |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix Q |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Q` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix Z |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `compq`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute Q;
  -   `= 'I'`: Q is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix Q is returned;
  -   `= 'V'`: Q must contain an orthogonal matrix Q1 on entry, and the product $Q_{1} \, Q$ is returned.
- `compz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute Z;
  -   `= 'I'`: Z is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix Z is returned;
  -   `= 'V'`: Z must contain an orthogonal matrix Z1 on entry, and the product $Z_{1} \, Z$ is returned.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `ihi`: `ILO` and `IHI` mark the rows and columns of A which are to be reduced. It is assumed that A is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N. `ILO` and `IHI` are normally set by a previous call to DGGBAL; otherwise they should be set to 1 and N respectively. $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `ILO=1` and `IHI=0`, if $N=0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N general matrix to be reduced. On exit, the upper triangle and the first subdiagonal of A are overwritten with the upper Hessenberg matrix H, and the rest is set to zero.
- `B`: On entry, the N-by-N upper triangular matrix B. On exit, the upper triangular matrix $T = Q^T$ B Z. The elements below the diagonal are set to zero.
- `Q`: On entry, if `COMPQ = 'V'`, the orthogonal matrix Q1, typically from the QR factorization of B. On exit, if `COMPQ='I'`, the orthogonal matrix Q, and if `COMPQ = 'V'`, the product $Q_{1} \, Q$. Not referenced if `COMPQ='N'`.
- `Z`: On entry, if `COMPZ = 'V'`, the orthogonal matrix Z1. On exit, if `COMPZ='I'`, the orthogonal matrix Z, and if `COMPZ = 'V'`, the product $Z_{1} \, Z$. Not referenced if `COMPZ='N'`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `ilo < 1`)
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `ihi > N \|\| ihi < ilo - 1`)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgghrd.strided(
    compq, compz,
    N,
    ilo, ihi,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `compq` | `"none" \| "initialize" \| "update"` | `'none'`, `'initialize'`, or `'update'` |
| `compz` | `"none" \| "initialize" \| "update"` | `'none'`, `'initialize'`, or `'update'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ilo` | `integer` | Ilo (1-based)<br>Rejects `ilo < 1` |
| `ihi` | `integer` | Ihi (1-based)<br>Rejects `ihi > N \|\| ihi < ilo - 1` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix A |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix B |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix Q |
| ↳ `strideQ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `strideQ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `offsetQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Q` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix Z |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Z` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `compq`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute Q;
  -   `= 'I'`: Q is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix Q is returned;

It is assumed that A is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N. `ILO` and `IHI` are normally set by a previous call to DGGBAL; otherwise they should be set to 1 and N respectively. $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `ILO=1` and `IHI=0`, if $N=0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N general matrix to be reduced. On exit, the upper triangle and the first subdiagonal of A are overwritten with the upper Hessenberg matrix H, and the rest is set to zero.
- `B`: On entry, the N-by-N upper triangular matrix B. On exit, the upper triangular matrix $T = Q^T$ B Z. The elements below the diagonal are set to zero.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `ilo < 1`)
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `ihi > N \|\| ihi < ilo - 1`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dgghrd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dgghrd';

// 3x3 general matrix A (column-major):
const A = new Float64Array([
	2.0,
	3.0,
	1.0,
	1.0,
	1.0,
	0.5,
	0.5,
	2.0,
	3.0
]);

// 3x3 upper triangular B (column-major):
const B = new Float64Array([
	1.0,
	0.0,
	0.0,
	0.5,
	2.0,
	0.0,
	0.25,
	1.0,
	3.0
]);

const Q = new Float64Array( 9 );
const Z = new Float64Array( 9 );

// Reduce (A, B) to generalized upper Hessenberg form:
const info = dgghrd( 'column-major', 'initialize', 'initialize', 3, 1, 3, A, 3, B, 3, Q, 3, Z, 3 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'A (Hessenberg):', A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'B (triangular):', B ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Q:', Q ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Z:', Z ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGGHRD`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGGHRD reduces a pair of real matrices (A,B) to generalized upper Hessenberg form using orthogonal transformations, where A is a general matrix and B is upper triangular. The form of the generalized eigenvalue problem is

$$
A \, x = \lambda \, B \, x
$$

and B is typically made upper triangular by computing its QR factorization and moving the orthogonal matrix Q to the left side of the equation.

This subroutine simultaneously reduces A to a Hessenberg matrix H:

$$
Q^T \, A \, Z = H
$$

and transforms B to another upper triangular matrix T:

$$
Q^T \, B \, Z = T
$$

in order to reduce the problem to its standard form

$$
H \, y = \lambda \, T \, y
$$

where $y = Z^T \, x$.

The orthogonal matrices Q and Z are determined as products of Givens rotations. They may either be formed explicitly, or they may be postmultiplied into input matrices Q1 and Z1, so that

$$
Q_{1} \, A \, Z_{1}^T = (Q_{1} \, Q) \, H \, (Z_{1} \, Z)^T
$$

$$
Q_{1} \, B \, Z_{1}^T = (Q_{1} \, Q) \, T \, (Z_{1} \, Z)^T
$$

If Q1 is the orthogonal matrix from the QR factorization of B in the original equation $A \, x = \lambda \, B \, x$, then DGGHRD reduces the original problem to generalized Hessenberg form.

### Further Details

This routine reduces A to Hessenberg and B to triangular form by an unblocked reduction, as described in \_Matrix\_Computations\_, by Golub and Van Loan (Johns Hopkins Press.)

</section>
